title: Private deploy midday sprint list
content:
Midday sprint notes — personal scratchpad (quick, noisy).

Context:
- Customer: FinCorp (EU region) — private VPC + on-prem inference nodes.
- Goal today: get first canary running behind customer ALB, validate KMS-wrapped model keys, and confirm eviction/backoff behavior under load.

Top of mind / today’s micro-goals:
- [ ] Confirm load-balancer healthchecks match runtime port (expected: 8081). last customer note said 8080.
- [ ] Run smoke canary (image tag rw-infer:onprem-2026-03-03-canary) against customer staging subnet (10.12.3.0/24).
- [ ] Validate KMS OK: key alias arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:999999999:key/abc-123 (ask SecOps if alias mismatch)
- [ ] Disk pressure check on node-02: ensure /var/lib/inference has > 50GB free before cache warmup.
- [ ] Update rollout policy to 10% -> 50% after memory profile looks stable for 15m.

Quick runbook snippets (notes to self):
- systemctl status redwood-inference && journalctl -u redwood-inference -n 200
- docker images | grep rw-infer && docker run --rm -e RW_ENV=stg \  
  -v /var/lib/inference:/cache rw-infer:onprem-2026-03-03-canary /bin/sh -c "/usr/local/bin/serve --port 8081"
- curl -sS http://10.12.3.45:8081/healthz  # expect 200 + json {"ok":true}

Noted blockers (open):
- Customer infra: outbound NAT gateway is restricted to 443 only. Need to confirm if control-plane callbacks (webhooks) can reach our ingestion endpoint; fallback plan is to proxy via customer jump-host.
- Node-02 reported nv_peer_mem driver mismatch with kernel 5.15. Need SRE to patch driver or provision new node with kernel 5.18.
- KMS rotation policy: customer rotates monthly — but current model key was created 2023 and shows "pending-rotation". Ask security to check decryption logs.

Observations from morning tests:
- Inference binary warms slower on small-batch workloads (latency spike first 50 tokens). Suspect cold KV-cache population; solution: prewarm with a short prefix request across all replicas.
- Batching config set to conservative default (max_batch_size: 8). For FinCorp workload (many short prompts ~32 tokens), bump to 16 and lower max_wait_ms to 8 to reduce tail latency (experiment).

Customer environment reminders (handy):
- Timezone: CET (UTC+1) / DST rules in effect — coordinate post-deploy checks 09:00-12:00 CET.
- Allowed IPs for management: 3.23.150.77, 52.17.12.9 (put in ticket to add if missing).
- Ops contact: +44 7700 900123 (Anita), Escalation: sec-ops-oncall@fincorp.com

Parking lot / non-blocking ideas:
- Try quantized variant on canary (int8 wheel) to see memory reduction; make note to measure perf delta and hallucination risk on our eval set.
- Add a pre-deploy script to check kernel compatibility and nvdriver before we schedule nodes. Could be small utility: rw-check-kernel.sh

Things I told customer in morning call (copyable):
- "We're targeting a phased canary today; you'll see a small percentage of traffic routed to the new cluster for ~30 minutes. We'll monitor latency and error rates and roll back automatically if the error rate crosses 1%."
- Asked for confirmation: "Can you enable temporary SSH from our jump-host IP for 2 hours?"

Immediate next steps (ordered):
1) Ping SecOps about KMS alias mismatch (quick slack: @secops-key).
2) Open infra ticket for NAT + ALB healthcheck port mismatch (JIRA-PI-3421 comment).
3) SSH to node-02, run dmesg | tail and check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log for driver errors; if kernel mismatch, toggle to fallback node-04.
4) Kick a 1-replica canary, run 100 short prefix requests, capture p99 latency and token throughput.
5) Share quick snapshot with solution owner (Jon R.) and ask for go/no-go on 50% increase.

Random micro-notes (messy):
- Remember: do not push canary image to prod registry tag; use ephemeral tag and delete after tests.
- If prewarm script spikes CPU, limit concurrency to 4/s.
- Check that metrics export uses correct tenant label (fincorp-tenant) or alerts will be noisy.

Open questions to follow up on:
- Does customer have strict egress rules that will block telemetry (prometheus push)? If yes, we need to set up a metrics-relay.
- Is the model pinned to a specific compilation kernel? (If yes, moving between node types may fail).

End-of-sprint note: breathing room at 15:40 CET, move to afternoon deep-dive on batching heuristics.

-- Asha
